v: Personally, I LOVED it!!! A simple revenge story gets Vikram Kumar’s special treatment, with Nani at his natural best and enough clever framing to reward viewers who enjoy something different.
e: GangLeader suffers mainly from the huge expectations created by Vikram Kumar and Nani joining hands. Taken on its own terms, though, the deliberately ordinary heroes and villain, subtle comedy and a handful of wonderfully staged scenes make the simple revenge story feel far more distinctive than its plot suggests.
body:
Personally, I loved the movie!!!

This time Vikram Kumar takes a simple revenge story and gives it his own special treatment.

There are about five scenes in particular — the opening, the interval framing, two moments in the second half and the post-climax reveal involving Sravani’s character — that really show the intelligence of the director 🙏

The biggest setback for the film is probably not the film itself, but the expectations surrounding it.

After Manam, and with a combination like Vikram Kumar and Nani, audiences naturally walk in expecting a highly intelligent and hugely entertaining thriller.

If you remove that burden and simply watch what is on screen, there is a lot to appreciate.

One of Vikram’s interesting choices is that none of the main characters is conventionally powerful — not even the villain.

That can be difficult for a regular audience used to the larger-than-life heroes and intimidating villains of Rajamouli- or Boyapati-style cinema.

But that lack of exaggerated power is also what gives this story its own flavour.

Nani is, as usual, at his natural best and completely submits himself to the character rather than trying to turn it into another star vehicle.

Anirudh’s BGM is trendy and works nicely with the mood, although I expected stronger songs from someone of his calibre.

Even with simple characters, a deliberately understated villain and fairly subtle comedy, the film manages to keep a grip on the audience.

This is strictly not for viewers looking for a powerful hero-villain clash or a full-length Nani comedy entertainer.

But audiences who enjoy slightly different genre films are much more likely to connect with what Vikram is trying to do here.

v: Man!!!! What a movie. Chhichhore deserves to sit beside Dil Chahta Hai, 3 Idiots and Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara — hilarious, emotional, wonderfully real and carrying a message that actually stays with you.
e: Chhichhore captures college friendships with characters who feel instantly familiar, then blends that nostalgia with a genuinely meaningful emotional message. Nitesh Tiwari and his writers balance comedy, sentiment and emotion in almost perfect proportions, creating the rare film whose effort and result are both complete successes.
body:
Man!!!! What a movie…

I am not exaggerating when I say Chhichhore has what it takes to sit in the same conversation as films like Dil Chahta Hai, 3 Idiots and Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara.

It has shades of all three, but it still stands on its own because of the emotional message it delivers and the wonderfully realistic way it portrays college life and friendships.

Almost every group of friends can identify an Anni, Sexa, Acid, Mummy or Bevda somewhere in its own history 😄

That familiarity makes the humour work even before the larger emotional story takes over.

Director Nitesh Tiwari and his team of writers do a fantastic job with the story, dialogues and screenplay.

Emotion, sentiment and comedy are mixed in almost perfect proportions.

The screenplay is especially strong because the film can move between laughter and pain without making either side feel artificial.

You come away feeling as though you watched an emotional comedy, a friendship film and a message-oriented drama at the same time — without any one ingredient crushing the others.

One line in the film essentially sums up the entire idea: your result does not decide whether you are a success or a failure; your effort does.

And in my view, the Chhichhore team succeeds on both counts.

They clearly put in the effort — and the result is outstanding too 🙏

v: Where does Ayushmann get the guts to keep picking these subjects? 😄 Raaj Shaandilyaa keeps the comedy spicy and witty without letting it become vulgar, while a terrific supporting cast sells every bit of the madness.
e: Dream Girl takes a premise that could easily have slipped into cheap or vulgar comedy and handles it with surprising control. Ayushmann is effortlessly convincing, Raaj Shaandilyaa’s writing keeps the jokes lively without crossing the line, and the supporting cast turns the unusual setup into a bright, accessible entertainer.
body:
Where does Ayushmann Khurrana get the guts to keep selecting such unconventional subjects — and then perform them so naturally and convincingly?!!!!!

He really does look like he is on the path to becoming one of Bollywood’s next big performers alongside Rajkummar Rao.

Story-wise, I felt the basic idea had a little flavour of Tumhari Sulu, except with Ayushmann effectively becoming the Pooja voice at the centre of the chaos.

This is also exactly the kind of premise that could have gone badly wrong.

If handled without control, the so-called decent family audience could easily have rejected it as vulgar comedy.

That is where debut director and writer Raaj Shaandilyaa shows his experience and talent.

The dialogues remain spicy and witty enough to keep the comedy alive, but they rarely cross the border into being unnecessarily vulgar.

Another masterstroke is the supporting cast.

The film surrounds Ayushmann with strong comic performers who understand how to deliver this material with exactly the right tone — naughty enough to be funny, but controlled enough to remain broadly watchable.

The BGM complements the mood very well, the couple of major songs fit the content nicely and the visuals stay bright and appealing.

The one drawback, if I have to pick one, is the heavy use of Haryanvi and Uttar Pradesh slang.

It gives the setting a much more realistic flavour, but audiences from other parts of the country may need a little extra effort to catch every line and enjoy the comedy as effortlessly as local viewers.

That is a relatively small limitation in an otherwise smartly handled and very entertaining comedy.

v: When three baaaps of MASS — Puri, Mani and Ram — come together, the result is an Isssssmartish BLOCKBUSTER! Sci-fi backdrop, full mass kick, Mani’s BGM and Ram’s mad energy… poyiiii kummundri!!!!!
e: iSmart Shankar is Puri Jagannadh going back to unapologetic mass cinema, this time with a sci-fi hook and Ram operating at absurd energy levels. The writing may not have Puri’s hardest-hitting dialogue, but Mani Sharma’s BGM, Ram’s performance and the director’s full-throttle attitude made this exactly the kind of mass feast I wanted.
body:
When three baaaps of MASS — Puri, Mani and Ram — come together… the result is an Isssssmartish BLOCKBUSTER 🙏

Puri Jagannadh chooses a completely massssssy movie with a sci-fi backdrop and, mannnn, he delivers!!!!!!

Being a Puriiii fan, I have enjoyed most of his earlier work, and this movie was no different for me.

If anything, Puri makes sure to add an extra dose of mass kick this time.

Dialogue-wise, this may not contain the kind of hard-hitting lines we associate with Puri at his very best, but he still throws in a few excellent mass dialogues at exactly the right moments.

Mani Sharma’s BGM is superb.

The climax score in particular gives you that instant HIGH the moment it kicks in!!!!!

And then there is Ram 🙏🙏

At times I genuinely wondered what he had taken to produce such a hyper-energetic performance 😄

He throws himself into the body language, slang and madness with zero hesitation.

Finally… aaadaaa Puri, Mani & Ram kalisi balisina potellani kosi… garam masala poosiiii… masth biryaniiii vandaaru!!!!!

Poyiiiii kummundri!!!!! 🔥
